guarantees.claim: On asynchronous reset (rst_ni low), err_q is cleared to 0.
On each posedge clk_i when rst_ni is high, if intg_err or reg_we_err is high, err_q is set to 1; otherwise it retains its previous value.

uncertain_points.claim: err_q is a sticky error bit that latches high on any error condition and is only cleared by hard reset. It is unclear whether this matches the intended register specification (e.g., if software is expected to clear it).
uncertain_points.cond: After an error event, while reset is inactive
uncertain_points.risk: If the design requires a software-clearable error status, missing a clear path could lead to missed error detection in subsequent operations or inability to distinguish new errors from past ones.

uncertain_points.claim: The severity of err_q's sticky-until-reset behavior depends on how it is consumed. If err_q feeds interrupt/alert logic, a missing clear mechanism might be acceptable only if the system is reset on alert; otherwise it could cause spurious or masked alerts.
uncertain_points.cond: When err_q is high and system not reset
uncertain_points.risk: Permanent assertion of an error signal due to lack of clear could break alert handling or mask new errors.
